Order No. 404-2572417-8110741 - Amazon ESI purchased a La Roche-Posay Anthelios Oil Correct SPF 50+ sunscreen from Amazon, a product I’ve been using for quite some time. As soon as I received it, I found the texture extremely runny, the color different, and it lacked the usual mattifying effect. I assumed it was a new formula from the brand — which does happen — and continued using it.However, after finishing that bottle, I bought the same product again, this time directly from a pharmacy. The difference is striking: color, texture, scent, skin feel, and the expected mattifying effect — everything was back to what I was used to. I then decided to compare the packaging: the product from Amazon is clearly counterfeit.Among several inconsistencies are:- The Amazon label says “50 spf” instead of “50+ spf”;- The color and size of the orange rectangle are different;- There is no batch number or expiration date printed on the packaging;- The font, printing, and finish differ from the original.The most serious part? The product was shipped directly by Amazon itself, not by a third-party seller.To make matters worse, when I tried to leave a negative review warning about the counterfeit product, Amazon censored my comment, claiming it violated their guidelines. In other words, they sell fake products, shipped by themselves, and hide legitimate customer reviews that warn other consumers.It is deeply concerning and unacceptable that a company the size of Amazon would be complicit in the distribution of counterfeit products, ignoring the real risks this poses to public health. This is not just a matter of a bad shopping experience, but one of responsibility and trust — fundamental pillars of a platform of this scale.

In July 2024, I purchased a "Canon Genuine Toner Cartridge 054H Black" from Amazon.  In less than six months, it started producing black vertical lines.  Since this was sold as a "genuine" Canon product, I called Canon support.  They were extremely helpful and determined that the toner cartridge was a counterfeit.  I filed a report with their anti-counterfeit department.When I called Amazon to report this is when the problems began.  The first time I called, the representative said that since the purchase was more than 120 days ago, there was nothing they could do.  Eventually, they offered a partial refund, which I told them was unacceptable.  After nearly 30 minutes on hold, I figured out the representative had disconnected the call.I called back.  I explained the situation and after another 20 minutes, this representative assured me that I would received a full credit to my Amazon account.The next morning, I received a notice from Amazon that a partial credit had been issued to my AMEX card.  So, I called back again, explaining that Amazon had sold me a counterfeit product which had been verified as such by the manufacturer.  Again, I got the 120 story and was told there was a "restocking fee."  I tried to explain that you cannot restock a counterfeit product and demanded a full refund.  It took me another 30 minutes, but I finally prevailed.Beyond the frustration of dealing with Amazon customer dis-service, at no time did any representative express concern about selling a counterfeit product or indicate that this would be reported within the company.  So the seller will likely continue to sell these toner cartridges.As it turns out, Amazon sells a lot of counterfeit toner cartridges.  This one came from the seller, Anurice Supplies.  Do not buy anything from this seller.  If you have, and it was marked as a Canon product, check the QR code square.  If it has boxes in three of the corners, according to Canon it is counterfeit.  Also look at the Canon name on the cartridge.  If it is painted on, it is a counterfeit.  There are other signs as well.This seller must be banned from Amazon immediately.  Their counterfeit product could have ruined my printer.   And, Amazon need to take immediate responsibility for these situations and make the customer whole without question.Shame on Amazon.  I'll never buy a toner cartridge from them again.

I have been using Amazon since 1999.  Since that time,  I have left very detailed and well written reviews.  So much so, that a few years ago I was invited to be one of Amazon's "Vine" reviewers.  These are reviewers who receive their choice of available free products from sellers to review.  I did this for a year until I found it to be not worth the time.My issues with Amazon however is this.First, the quality of their items, shipping, packing, and oversight of their third party system is terrible.  I am disabled and rely upon ordering online for almost everything I need.  As such, at one time it was typical of me to order from Amazon two or more times a week. When I order, I also spend amazing amounts of time with reviews before purchasing, going through Amazon's barely useful search system to compare prices, and other things.Because of my very frequent and long years of using Amazon's website, I have become aware of some rather disingenuous and downright deceptive ways in which their site functions.  For one, you cannot nor should depend upon the default "Top Reviews" as they appear.  They are essentially useless, especially today and with products that have been available on Amazon for a few years.  These reviews are often outdated and do no reflect the current status of either the product, its quality changes, or even Amazon's shipping issues, amongst other things.It is best to change that default to "Recent Reviews".  That is where you will see the most revealing and often disheartening reviews about a product. And it won't matter much whether it is a big name brand or not.  As in the past ten years, many long existing companies have reduced many aspects of their manufacturing to garner higher and higher profits at your expense.  As a result their products may look good (as modern manufacturing and design can definitely make them, especially with current plastic extrusion molding methods), the fact is they are made far cheaper, reduced quality control, and with planned obsolescence in mind.  It is no joke, no fantasy, but a real situation.It is here you will also discover a trend that has arisen with Amazon in the past five years as well.  The number of used, returns, and possibly seconds being sold as brand new by Amazon is astounding.  That and their shoddy packing due to the low moral, sad working conditions, etc., of their packers affects the way items eventually reach you.Word of warning.  If you change the default of "Recent Reviews" too often, that function will vanish from the review section.  It is the only element on Amazon's product pages that does this (aside from frequent price changing).  But take heart, you only need reload the page a few times and it will return.  It is a headache, but that is the point.  To dissuade you from being able to see the actuality of what the situation is with what you are purchasing.As for the countless items from China available on Amazon, be forewarned.  These exact same items are being sold directly out of China on Temu, AliExpress, and elsewhere.  However, Amazon is charging on average two to four times more for them.  In fact I included this information in a review of a product I purchased from Amazon, only to have my review privileges revoked.  That was two years ago. And since, I can no longer leave reviews, nor even contact sellers to inquire about specific questions about a product. According to Amazon, I have gone against their "Community Standards".Community Standards?Read those words and let them sink in for a moment to understand their irony.As a result, I no longer use Amazon unless I have absolutely no alternative.  The first reason being that over the past two years, two out of three orders are problematic.  Either the item is wrong, broken, expired, damaged, extremely late, etc.Second, since I've discovered that so much of what Amazon sells is actually from China, and they are now selling directly to us for far lower prices, why continue ordering from Amazon?  Especially in those cases, when the quality may not be up to specs, are fakes or knock-offs (and yes, they are on Amazon), only to pay so much more for them?  For the three day delivery of Prime, which unless it is delivered by Amazon, is anything but three day.No.  That is silly.  And the argument that you are supporting your nation's brand is even more ludicrous.  First, Amazon has a horrible labor reputation.  Second, Amazon is the Walmart of the internet retail business and as such has systematically worked to dominate as many retail industries it can move into and all for the sole purpose of driving everyone else out of business, which it has done since the the late 1990s.Jeff Bezo's its CEO/Founder is now one of the wealthiest men in world. In fact, him, Musk, and Zuckerberg have more wealth than the entire bottom half of the U.S., population.

People please! Think and take your time with your post. You hurt people's minds trying to read your post, using poor grammar! One of the biggest reasons for a misdelivery, is poor shipping labels! The type print is to small. The name of the recipient along with their numbered street address has to be big and bold. The most pronounced of any type print on the label. I use to service people in the delivery sector. While loading and separating parcels by street for delivery, we did so under unfavorable lighting and weather conditions. With type print of the name and address so small you could not make out the correct address and name unless it was under direct sunlight. Then you see those small 6's were actually 8"s etc. and those f's were actually p's etc. Even natural lighting coming in to the drivers window is not enough because of the small print. The type print of the name and address has to be the biggest on the label to dramatically cut down on misdeliveries. Also products that were not packaged securely by the shipper broke open during handling, leaving some or all of their content in the deliverers hamper ( a big cart to hold their packages for the day ) thus requiring the carrier ( driver ) to turn in the loose contents at the bottom of their hamper to the supervisor as lost product. Many times not knowing what parcels were with or were without full or partial content. Then we would have to wait on the customer to call about their missing contents and try to match them up with our lost and found contents. So for every ones sake. Have your street address clearly legible. There is way to many faded and partially blocked numbers on people's addresses. For those who live on corners where their house faces the front, (yet due to incompetent city planners assigning them the side street name) put your street name just below your numbered address. Finally secure those shipments!  Handlers and delivers of those packages are not going to treat them like a new born baby, yet more like a sack of potatoes. As for Amazon they fared much better in delivery accuracy, when they used by deception, the US Postal service for delivery as they quietly got their logistics up and running. After using and dumping the Postal service, which bent over backwards in giving them excellent priority in service and price, you will be fortunate to receive your delivery or misdelivery of your neighbors shipment by the same Amazon driver within the same week.

On the one hand, I don't want to criticize the majority of Amazon warehouse workers who are most likely working under enormous pressure, and trying to do their best to ensure that customers receive much-needed products in a safe and timely manner. To those workers, Kudos! And I give them my sincere heart-felt thanks.But to the select few who maybe belong to the "it's just a job, so I don't care what I do" camp, LISTEN UP! No more lame excuses -- use some common sense and do a decent job! Pack boxes in the way that YOU or your mother or your own grandmother would like to receive them! Don't pack them with the expectation that if things arrive damaged and broken that it is somebody else's fault -- it's not! It's the fault of the person doing the packing. Period!Dear Readers... please bear in mind that the situation that I am about to describe is the same kind of careless, senseless 'service' that had been happening long before Covid-19 came around and complicated things for everybody.Case in point: I ordered a food processor that probably weighs somewhere between 20-25 lbs. It has a plastic bowl and plastic attachments that are regarded as reasonably fragile. I purchased it as a replacement for one I'd had for decades that suddenly quit, ironically right at the time of pandemic when I would be cooking at home even more! Given the rather delicate nature of the some of the machine's components, I ordered the item solo, with the expectation that nothing else would be shipped in the same box with it.Never mind the fact that the food processor arrived almost 3 weeks late for a Prime Order, given that Amazon has recently prioritized deliveries of what it considers 'essential' products. (Also never mind the fact that at Amazon, a DVD can be shipped and arrive in less than a week, but that a cooking appliance is not considered 'essential' or essential enough.) The food processor wasn't scheduled for delivery for another couple of days.Imagine my surprise when I saw a HUGE box on our porch -- Yippee! Maybe such a large box means that someone in an Amazon warehouse cared enough to pack it well? NOT.Also inside the box was a recent order for 12 cans of soup! The heavy soup cans were wedged on top of the food processor and shoved so tightly against that the round outline of the rim on one of the soup cans was embossed into the cardboard box the processor comes in! The huge brown shipping box had a scant amount of flimsy brown packing paper inside.The irony in all of this is that when I ordered the soup, I made certain to order it solo also, to make certain that soup cans wouldn't go into a box with other things! I was concerned about how heavy 12 cans of soup would be to carry. So let's see... 16 oz. cans... 12 of them... and a 20+ lb food processor... so something like 37 lbs in a big box ... Thank God that we got the box into the house safely.Yet I wonder who in their right mind would put a heavy flat of canned soup on top of a food processor with an acrylic bowl, that just so happens to be packed right at the top of the appliance box. How is that? Seems more like a case "Let's just hurry up" and "we don't give a tinker's you-know-what" than mere stupidity, but who knows?The situation also makes me wonder why it took so long to get the food processor in the first place. Were they just waiting to send it until we ordered something else? Funny that it showed up 2 days earlier in the same box with another order that it wasn't supposed to be matched with!God Bless all the hard-working folks at Amazon. I really do appreciate them. For the others ... may God give them the graces they need to do their jobs with integrity and a little more common sense.

We all know what Amazon does: An incredible breadth of products, great prices, and free or cheap delivery. I've been a customer for 18 years, and a prime customer for a few years.No longer. In early 2016, they switched from using actual delivery services, such as USPS, FedEx or UPS, to their own, farmed-out service, "Amazon Logistics." Make no mistake, Amazon Logistics is not part of Amazon. It consists entirely of Uber-like drivers in your local area. If you have a white Ford Econoline van, you can be "Amazon Logistics" tomorrow. And if you can hire a couple of homeless guys to drive the vans, you can actually make some money.Unfortunately, you get what you paid for. These homeless drivers can't find addresses, don't know how to navigate streets, and sure as heck aren't bonded, so gated communities, condos, apartment complexes, etc, are not going to give them keys -- in stark contrast to UPS, USPS, FedEx, etc. My previous ~800 purchases delivered via those big three were all perfect, except for one. My 12 or so deliveries since they switched to Amazon Logistics have been 0-12.Customer service is useless. Yes, I've been credited for all of the botched deliveries. But it's confusing as to why a company that is so focused on customer service, and renowned for its efficiency, would all of a sudden entrust the final mile of the process to... anyone. Literally, anyone; no background check, no bonding, no verification of insurance, anything.I cancelled my Prime membership as a result, and got the canned "sorry to see you go," email.Amazon's own discussion forum has over 1,000 complaints about Amazon Logistics, and form my research, not a single positive post. Yet Amazon seems to be willing to let those thousands (and many, many more who don't post) wander away, in order to save a few pennies. So be it.

I've been shopping on Amazon.com since they first came about (1994?) - and for the most part, they are fantastic. Every once in a while, a package arrives a date later than it should have - not the end of the world...I do have a few specific gripes, though. Why do they not have parental controls on Amazon Music Unlimited yet? This seems absolutely ridiculous to me - and if you do a quick Google search on this topic, you'll see a massive amount of unhappy people complaining. For parents, this is an absolute necessity, and a bizarre oversight on Amazon's part. My other issue is with Amazon Fresh. First of all, the price. Holy cow. It's a great convenience, but all the other local grocery delivery services are far cheaper. Also, it always seems like something goes wrong with these deliveries; whether it's all four of my bread items expire in three days from the delivery date, or half my order is delivered on time, but the other half is off in outer space and nobody can seem to track it down...I just can't figure out why these things aren't fixed by now. Train your people correctly. Track your deliveries. Easy stuff for a giant like Amazon.Other than those things, Amazon has been my favorite go-to online shopping place for many, many years, and I can't imagine it ever being replaced. Their customer service reps almost always fix your issues, and generally go above what you expected as a remedy. Their prices are almost always the best around (and you can always track prices via camel camel camel).

Be careful of anything coming from China, etc., especially clothing. If it's not eligible for fast shipping, it's coming from overseas and the quality (and sizing, color, material... and pretty much everything else you can think of) is not going to be as expected. Also, the return policy will be impossible (you'll have to pay massive shipping fees to send it back, assuming they even allow returns).  But for anything we've ordered that was here in the US, we've pretty much always been pleased, whether it was books, electronics, or something else.Also, do check the star ratings of the seller. If you stick with sellers who have sold a lot of things and who still have a high rating, they should be pretty dependable.

Throwing in items from multiple orders into a box is actually wrong, I've learned this from an Amazon rep. Doing so will not only ensure that you will NOT get a timely refund, but it creates more work for the people in the Amazon returns department who then have to manually look through your entire order history and match them up. In a busy work environment nobody wants to have to do that.Another thing that people seem to be missing: when returning an item pack the items CAREFULLY. You can initiate a return for a defective/unwanted product, but if the Amazon workers open up your box and find that it is damaged, they will NO LONGER refund you, they have implemented this policy a few years back. So make sure you pack your items carefully. Don't just toss them in a box without any cushioning/padding and then call it a day.Another thing that I've seen too many Amazon shoppers do is that they FAIL to read reviews before purchasing. That item is 3 stars for a reason! Don't just buy it because it looks like it works/is authentic. Too often I'm seeing people write negative reviews for an already terrible product because they failed to read the reviews. The reviews are there for a reason, and should guide you in your purchase making. It's like buying the first car you see because you like the way it looks, then coming back to the dealership the next day because you discovered that you're too small/big to fit properly in the driver's seat. Be a SMART buyer, not a DUMB one.As a suggestion, Amazon needs to invest in a 'cooling warehouse' for perishable products such as skincare, which lose their efficacy by a large margin when exposed to heat. A few weeks ago I finally decided to take the plunge and purchase a sewing machine, for those of you who don’t know, this isn’t a cheap purchase by any means. So to save a few dollars I buy a factory refurbished model being sold by Amazon, great reviews, all the bells and whistles, and roughly $150 worth of included accessories. Order showed up a day early and I’m super excited to set it up and start figuring this machine out, but much to my disappointment when I unpacked the box none of the accessories were there except for one, or so I thought. In my disappointment I started a return when I was offered a replacement item to be shipped to me next day and I had a month to return to one I had with missing pieces for free, using a UPS pickup, just had to confirm that it I didn’t return the item the full cost would be charged to my original payment method, which couldn’t happen, this was a splurge, but since I was absolutely returning it I wasn’t worried about this and agreed. Since I was bored and decided that I could still mess around with the machine without the optional accessories that were to be included I set it up and started reading through the manual when in it I discovered basically a hidden storage compartment in the base of the machine. Open it up and ta-da there’s my “missing” accessories. So I hurry up and try to cancel the replacement but it has already shipped so I can’t, okay no problem I’ll just return it when it gets here. While laughing with my mom about my little blonde moment she mentions that she would like to learn to sew and wants to buy this machine off of me, okay no problem I just have to get ahold of Amazon and have them change the payment method they will charge when I don’t return it since I didn’t want the charge on a credit card. Contact CS through the chat feature and explain that I no longer wish to return either machine and that I need to pay for the replacement one but need to change my payment method. CS Rep asks me to wait for a few moments while she sees if this is something she can do, when she responds she says that she is unable to change the payment method after an order has been placed, but that I haven’t been charged. Confused at this point I tell her I know I haven’t been yet because I was to return one machine but that I will no longer be returning it and I agreed to be charged the full amount for both if I didn’t send one back and that I was just trying to pay for the second machine. At this point she tells me she understands all of this, and that what she was trying to say is that she will switch the replacement to a return so that I can keep both machines and not be charged for the second one. At this point I’m floored, but this was my mistake, and I’m not trying to not pay for it, I just want to use a different card to pay for it, why should Amazon give me a free machine just because I can’t change a payment method on a machine I wouldn’t have even needed shipped to me had I dug a little deeper in search of the accessories? Again she confirms that I can keep both machines with no charge for the second machine, also that she will send me email confirmation of this at my request, just in case a charge shows up on my card because this seems to good to be true. Within 30 seconds of ending the chat I have email confirmation of keeping both machines and not being charged for the second one. Wow. Thank you Amazon, you made myself and my mother very very happy yesterday. Never would have dreamed I would end up with a free mid level Brother sewing machine by contacting Amazon in an attempt to PAY for said sewing machine just because they don’t have the ability to change my payment method. Still in shocked disbelief, I guess the karma gods were happy with me yesterday.

Generally speaking Chrono24 is a good site. As one of the world's biggest sites for pre-owned watches, the selection on offer is very good — and their escrow payment service makes transactions safe and easily handled. All good so far.Where Chrono24 falls short is on communication, fees and "sales tricks".1. CommissionThey charge a 6.5-8.5% fee on transactions — resulting in exorbitant fees on more expensive watches, when all they really do is offer a decent platform and a holding account for transactions. That's too much, and they are ripe for more competition because of this.2. ValuationsIn your so-called "watch collection" (a list of the watches you own), Chrono24 will value your watch at a certain price, which may lead you to think it has gone up in value. But when you actually go to sell it, Chrono24 recommends it goes on the market for a much lower price. As an example, a watch "valued" at 11,500 was a minute later recommended by Chrono24 to go on the market for 9,400, when I went to sell it. This reflects very badly on Chrono24.3. CommunicationYou can contact Chrono24 via various forms on the site, but I am yet to receive an answer to any of my questions. I have written them three times.4. Currency exchange ratesChrono24 will user their "own" currency exchange rate if you, say, accept an offer made in British pounds. Chrono24 will always want payment in Euro, which is fine, but you will pay a premium of around 2.5% for Chrono24 to settle with the seller in another currency. Chrono24's incurred fees when paying the seller in, say, pounds will by much, much smaller, so this is a "hidden" fee on top of the already high fee. Very poor service.5. On-site marketing spamThe platform will bombard you with pop-ups asking you to create "alerts", review sellers etc. etc. while you are browsing. You can close them, but on the next page load another one will load. It is quite absurd and significantly detracts from the experience on their site.In sum, it's an efficient platform for its purpose, and since it's so dominant on the market, it's hard to avoid it if you are into watches. But I hope someone will soon launch an alternative with fewer irritants, more transparency and more reasonable fees.

This is what union solidarity looks like! With eBay-owned gaming company TCGPlayer continuing to stall and delay bargaining and throwing every union-busting tactic in the book at the workers, several workers - members of CWA Local 1123 - traveled from Syracuse, NY to Las Vegas in late September to put eBay on blast for their illegal union-busting - and they had help from a huge showing of support by our CWA Local 9413 family.CWAers picketed outside the Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, where the Workday Rising Conference was being held, to tell Workday CFO and eBay Board Member Zane Rowe to put an end to eBay’s union-busting and settle this contract now.“We are here in Las Vegas to let Zane Rowe know that what happens in Syracuse doesn’t stay in Syracuse,” said Tyler, an Inventory Specialist at TCGplayer. “We’re fighting for the pay, benefits, and protections we deserve.”The CWA 1123-TCGUnion members - the first group of eBay workers to unionize - have been fighting for their first union contract since early 2023, but have faced egregious union-busting from the company in the form of cutting benefits, delaying union recognition, and multiple federal labor law violations. But the workers are standing firm and refusing to back down against the Goliath commerce company - and it helps to know that our union family throughout the country has our members’ backs!TCGplayer Workers Rally to Call Attention to eBay's Worker ExploitationOn October 2nd CWA Local 1123-TCGUnion members rallied in Syracuse, NY to highlight the inexcusably low wages made by workers and demand that eBay and its subsidiary company TCGplayer bargain in good faith and agree to reasonable contract terms, including meaningful wage increases.On the same day, CWA launched the “Tapped Out at TCGplayer” report, showing how eBay are struggling to make ends meet - even as eBay boast about their net worth of $31 billion. The majority of eBay Authentication Center workers in Syracuse earn less than a living wage for a single person without children.“Workers in Syracuse have shown incredible strength in their fight for fair pay and dignity in the workplace," said Chris Ryan, President of CWA Local 1123. "As one of the state’s largest employers, eBay and TCGplayer have quickly become a drain on our local economy by failing to pay workers livable wages and forcing them to rely on public assistance. eBay must bargain in good faith with its workers and raise the wages at TCGplayer, and I’m proud to stand in solidarity with CWA-TCGunion members in their efforts."TCGplayer is one of the largest online marketplaces for verification services, card games, and collectible trading cards. Workers are responsible for ensuring that every shipment in and out of TCGplayer’s hub in Syracuse is completed accurately and meets quality standards.TCGplayer workers won their union election in March 2023 and are the first group of eBay workers to win union recognition. In response to this victory, eBay and TCGplayer launched an anti-union campaign, hiring union-busting firm Littler Mendelson and engaging in a series of illegal delay tactics to avoid contract negotiations.“Today’s rally is about more than just pay—it’s about dignity, respect, and being able to support our families," said Megan Wheeler, eBay worker and CWA Local 1123-TCGunion member. "We come to work every day to make TCGplayer what it is today, but it’s impossible to make ends meet on the wages we’re earning. We, the workers of CWA-TCGunion, are sending a message to eBay: we deserve to be treated fairly and we deserve livable wages, and we won’t back down until we secure a contract that reflects that."The workers were joined at the rally by Citizen Action of NY, the NY Working Families Party, and elected officials including NY State Senator Rachel May and representatives from the offices of NY State Senator John Mannion and Senator Chuck Schum

The buy it now option was small fee option originally, but I use it for every item now for free.Another thing I love is to be able to send offers to watchers using that option. I have managed to earn sales myself by offering the item slightly cheaper than its listing price.The app itself is quite good, your page is clear by listing all your items and separating them into what’s active, sold, or unsold. As well as showing offers etc.I have some negatives, the first would be the fees eBay charge. They have the highest fee of all the selling apps and the fee is consistent regardless of how much the item sold for. For example, if I sold an item for £2 and I sold another for £200 the fee is the same and that becomes slightly disheartening on more expensive items that eBay take a lot away from you.Fees also have seemed to increase from my first month of selling to what they are now. I believe when I first started, they were around 10% but my last invoice showed fees of 12.5%. I can only assume that is because I sell more items than I did then but personally, I don’t think it should matter.I think it is very greedy of eBay to take a fee on the postage price, even if you use Royal Mail or Hermes etc. The fee should be for the item itself; eBay are not getting involved in the delivery.Its method of dealing with multiple items is very dated and time consuming. I have had many users purchase multiple items and ask for combined postage. Whilst, I have no issue with that, I must use a computer to manually make an invoice. If I am at work or simply not home, the buyer must wait until I get home to use a computer because this cant be done via the app. Vinted has automatic options in place when a seller wishes to purchase multiple items, the seller is sent a “Bundle Request” which they must approve the postage for. Depop has an automatic system in place that a seller can select to combine postage, refuse it, or even apply free postage on multiple items. It’s a lot easier for both parties than what eBay offers.I have had a few disputes with eBay, I won’t go into them all but due to the way eBay handled them it allows me to believe the following. I have read forums about eBay and many sellers say that over the years the attitude has changed from eBay being impartial and doing its part to protect sellers as well as buyers to now seeming to side with buyers. From the few disputes I have had, it came across to me that eBay didn’t seem to care and simply sided with the buyer because that is easier. I had a buyer create a case asking for a refund stating that he didn’t receive his item, I later found out that he was based in Malta, paid via the US eBay website but he had his item sent to Northern Ireland. I gave eBay the Royal Mail reference number which showed the item was delivered to the address he gave but eBay sided with the buyer and gave a refund by taking the money from my PayPal account before I even knew what they had done. I spent a long time speaking to eBay about the matter, but they didn’t seem to care. In the end I lost my item and eBay gave me the bill, despite I proved that the buyer had committed fraud.Overall, I have mixed feelings on eBay, it definitely has positives and perks but I feel that the company itself has taken a safer/greedier path of siding with buyers despite the fact they make their money from sellers with high fees.

They have fantastic prices, which is why I go back.  But customer service and shipping delays are where I have an issue.  I receive some orders with no issues at all.  But I have also had numerous instances where:1. I have placed orders, and a label has been created.  But then I have waited 10 days or more for them to ship.  Even though my account says "shipped," the tracking number says USPS doesn't have possession.  It's not shipped if USPS doesn't have it.2. I place an order and the order is unfulfilled for 10-14 days - no label, no updates, etc.In both instances, when I have reached out to customer service, there is suddenly movement.  Either the shipping label is created (once, I received notice of label creation while I was *on the chat*), or the item suddenly shows up at the USPS.And sometimes, they don't even respond to my inquiry.  The item just shows up at the USPS and their system sends me an automated email that the item is on the way.Most recently, I ordered Christmas gifts almost a month before Christmas.  I waited two business weeks for the package to ship.  No notification from the company about any kind of delay.  I sent an inquiry.  Within 24 hours, the package is at the USPS.From their policy: "Orders placed before 1:30 PM Eastern Standard Time on a business day will be processed and shipped out on the same day, provided that the ordered goods are in stock and customer identification is verified."So.  If the delay is caused by an item not being in stock, one of two things should happen 1) you shouldn't be able to place an order for out-of-stock items 2) but if you do, you should be notified that the item is out of stock and that you order is delayed.Otherwise, according to their policy, it should be shipped out the same day.Emails have dates, and so does the USPS tracking system.  Screenshots will clearly show the number of days the order date in my account and my email inquiry.  It will also show the date/time correlation between my inquiry, an email from the company that the item is on the way, and the receipt of the package by the USPS (*actual* shipment).And I can show this not once.  Not twice.  But numerous times.So now I know better than to just let my orders sit.  So my best advice is that if you order from them, just keep your eye on your tracking until you see USPS has your box.  And if it's been significantly past the number of business days stated in their shipping policy, reach out.  Shop.  But be vigilant.While I really appreciate the immediate response when they realize they haven't shipped my item, the bigger concern is whether the item would have shipped at all if I hadn't inquired.This is a respectful *but honest* review.  If the company responds to this post by gaslighting, being retaliatory, or downplaying the issue, here's what I have to say to you, my fellow consumer: "I rest my case."

In my case, I received the 4000USD watch with original box timely, just lack of manufacture's certificate (which has been claimed on jomashop). The first time round, I found a watch online and had it sent to the Mayfair office in order to view my desired purchase. As this is a premise as opposed to a shop, I had to make an appointment and there was a certain premium feeling I got from this visit. It was personal, intimate and very private. The second time I was looking for a watch, I had it sent to the store in Bluewater. This is an actual store, and this store is very small. When you enter, you are pretty much at the counter. It felt like a 12”x9” box room. There’s an armchair in one corner. Understandably, security is a concern when presenting the watches to clients, but I found it quite bizarre that I was about to complete a purchase for a considerable amount whilst standing. It was very transactional as opposed to interactional. Even though the given parameters pose unique challenges, I feel that there are thing that can be done to make purchases more personal and memorable.This time round I was part exchanging a watch, and i has already received a valuation online. I was a little shocked that the manager in store was unable to give me a form valuation and was trying to get hold of someone off site to confirm the value. Being a bank holiday, this was not possible so I left without completing my transaction. From my understanding, I believe My part exchange would have needed to be sent away for an inspection prior to secures deal anyway. So I wasted a lot of time Standing around whilst the Manager was trying to get a response from this person off site. In the end, I had my part exchange sent away for an inspection so we could move on. The sale was then finalised via phone and email. It all felt a little “clunky” and i suppose I didn’t expect this after the first experience I’d had. Possibly, sign posting how things work would’ve helped to manage my expectations. All in all, my experience was ok and I would use Watchfinder again but I probably would look elsewhere first. Or, view items at an alternative location. I love my watch, but I was Left feeling a little flat.

I ordered a fairly expensive watch from Watchfinder and initially all good - an easy transaction and once I had paid received a phone call within 2 hours asking for a delivery address and was told the watch would arrive before 1PM the next day.  As promised my new watch arrived the next day, well packaged and even though it did not have the original box the watchfinder replacement is well up to the task and looks to be reasonable quality.My first concern came when I examined the watch a bit more closely - the case was full 18K gold and had obviously been polished vigorously to the point where the model number and other engravings on the back of the watch had almost been polished off.  Not too much of an issue but certainly OTT.  I had asked about service history and was told it had been fully serviced with a few parts replaced prior to dispatch.Unfortunately in the space of 12 hours the watch had gained almost 2 hours.  Being a Swiss chronometer this is not good.  I complained to Watchfinder and they did agree to the watch being returned and wanted it to go back to their service department to be checked - to be honest I had little confidence in them at this point as how could a watch (expensive or not) be shipped with such a massive time gain?  According to their web site every watch is inspected and checked for condition and accuracy - obviously not in this case.They suggested that if I returned the watch it would go to their 'chief watch engineer' for inspection which begs the question as to who worked on it originally.It's difficult to criticise WatchFinder as in their defence they have cancelled the transaction and are in the process of refunding my money - they are also supposed to refund the postage costs to return it to them but on the other hand it's very poor to have a watch sent out in the first place in such condition and does not bode well for the quality of the rest of the work supposedly done to the watch.Update 15 December - they have gone down further as they don’t seem to even be able to get a refund sorted.  They received the watch back on the 5th and still have not refunded my £3500.  Simply not good enough that these companies can delay refunding for faulty goods.

Got an offer via email on a watch that was reasonable, and so was invited to pop in to their London "purchasing office" in the prestigious Burlington Arcade, so they could inspect the watch to seal the deal. I subsequently did so, and it was remarkable at how incongruous the service I was greeted with was, in the context of the luxury market these guys are looking to serve.I can't remember the name of the chap I was dealing with, and wouldn't name names even if I could, however I can tell you that no respect for the timepiece was made (this is a £16k+ retail watch, mind you; not chump change, at least to me!); box and papers treated roughly in front of me, handling of the watch was abrupt and disconcerting (relative to how I would/do, and I treat other's possessions even more carefully than my own so expect the same when someone else is handling my property), no gloves or such being worn when handling the watch (just a small thing, but if you want to be professional...), and returning it with time and date changed from what it was when I handed it over; I found it all incredibly odd.Beyond this, and I can assure you I'm not a paranoid snowflake(!), I was genuinely worried when he was looking at it under the light/magnification (back at his desk a little away from the seating area, though I could hear and observe through the holes in the divider), on account of his fumbling, knocking items around on his desk and onto the floor, all the while handling my expensive timepiece.Whilst no one thing may be particularly egregious, the litany of small transgressions rendered an overwhelmingly unprofessional feeling, and one I was happy to have gotten out of with my watch thankfully unscathed.Icing on the cake was that the fellow came back having affirmed the quality and condition of the watch after inspection, yet indicated that he'd still need to send it off to the main office for a final offer (5 working days and shipping it to another part of the country), despite the very fact I personally popped in explicitly to avoid the need for this and to receive an immediate offer.My advice wouldn't necessarily be to stay away from WF&Co in total, but if you do decide to chance a Burlington Arcade visit to sell a watch, communicate clearly your expectations around how your timepiece is handled, and keep it within sight at all times! But really, if my experience is anything close to normal, it's probably worth just sending it to their main office rather than faffing around with the amateurs in their London 'purchasing but I'm not really given any actual authority to make a purchasing decision' office.. that is, if you're willing to put your timepiece in the post and have it separated from you without a firm offer or guarantee of superlative handling/insurance whilst in their possession for potentially weeks. (I wasn't.)

It was an ok experience. I feel regarding the selling of watches no matter how good the condition, how much original paperwork you have, you will always be offered the lower value.

The buying experience itself was excellent - sales guy Michael Bergin was amazing, really friendly, very informative and the whole purchasing process was easy and straight forward and best of all secure. I come through London on business, so my biggest issue is partially due to not being resident in London.The issues...1) The process of trading in a watch here requires the watch being sent to Watchfinder in advance.  It is effectively a multi-day process, which is very inefficient and problematic for someone lacking several days in London, or who may not want to spend the money or go through the hassle of sending the watch by courier in advance.  I would rather live with some ambiguity about trade-in value for a couple days in exchange for the convenience of a single visit and transaction.  There must be a way!2)  It is very much "Buyer Beware" here.  Unlike other dealers, Watchfinder does not give a detailed condition report online, which puts the burden of selection in advance on the buyer.  Fine, but how to narrow a selection down?  For example, say I'm interested in a Rolex Submariner.  There are dozens available over Watchfinder's 4-5 locations.  How is one to narrow it down to 3-4 watches to view without knowing much about the condition of any of them?  Then those watches need to be sent to a single location for viewing, by arrangement.  Fingers crossed it all works out for the allotted day and time.3) Related point...  unexpected scratches and other imperfections are often found when actually inspecting a watch (bring a Loup!) which can lead to a wasted visit.  Condition reports could reduce or eliminate wasted visits. I know I need a clean bezel, but I can live with scratches on the case.  Simple things like this.4) Lastly, the sales staff on hand has varying degrees of industry and brand knowledge.  Don't go there for advice.The combination of all these points means that successfully conducting a trade-in and purchase with Watchfinder may be less likely or more complicated than with other dealers.Aside from and despite these points, the Watchfinder team was friendly and worked hard to handle my partial trade-in fairly.  It took several weeks, dozens of emails, and two trips to London, but the end result was satisfactory.  I got the watch I wanted, in (almost) the condition I hoped for, at a reasonable price.  The trade-in value on my watch was also fair.Another complimentary point:  Watchfinder deals in a wider variety and range of watches than many other 2nd hand dealers.I will do business with them again, certainly for certain brands, and am now more aware of the logistics involved in partial trade-ins.

With all the good feedback for Watchfinder on Trustpilot I'm not comfortable writing this feedback but it's a true representation of my experience, upto this point, if things change I will reflect those changes accordinglyDuring a trip to London I popped into Watchfinder in the Royal Exchange in order to get a better feel for them after reading some not so good feedback elsewhere on the internet(reviewcenter). The staff in the shop were friendly, polite and helpful which gave me confidence I could go home and buy from Watchfinder over the phone once I'd checked watches for sale online. I part exchanged my 2001 steel/gold blue Rolex Submariner for a 2014 steel Rolex Submariner with ceramic bezel. First I had to send my watch in using Special Delivery with max £2500 insurance selected which covered less than half the value of the watch but took the risk, though I don't know if I would again, it was a relief when Watchfinder confirmed it's arrival next day. Watchfinder have been friendly, polite and understanding throughout this sale. After completing the sale I realised the pictures used on the Watchfinder website to advertise the watch I'd purchased showed black deposits in some of the engraved bezel markers, I highlighted this to the sales rep who sold me the watch he agree'd it wasn't right and promised it would be cleaned properly prior to dispatch. The dispatch team called me before dispatch to confirm my delivery address at which point I mentioned cleaning of the bezel engravings to be informed it had been cleaned and was now spotless.I waited in anticipation for delivery this morning when it did arrive it was well packaged.  Once unwrapped my enjoyment of receiving my prestige watch was somewhat diminished when I realised the bezel hadn't been cleaned properly as promised on two occasions, at this point I took a number of photo's and sent them to Watchfinder. To my absolute dismay Watchfinder suggested I send it back to them for refund, cleaning or a watch with a clean bezel which not only exposed me to £11+ postage cost more importantly it exposed me to being under insured if the watch was lost in transit, Watchfinder wrongly advised the uninsured £2750 would be covered by my house insurance. They are WRONG to say this as the majority of house insurance policies have endorsements for high risk high value items which say in the case of a watch it's only covered whilst being worn by you or at least in your person or deposited in the bank or at home in a safe meaning it won't be covered if lost in the post. With this in mind sending it back to Watchfinder isn't an option unless they provide full insurance cover which some watch retailers offer but Watchfinder don't.I purchased the 6mth old Rolex based on the description on the Watchfinder website and paid a price in anticipation of it arriving in as described condition. I have explained my concern over returning it partially insured but Watchfinder insist I return the watch to them under insured. As I write this I'm in a catch 22 situation I have to risk under insured postage and potentially lose £2750 if the watch is lost which isn't an option for me or try and clean it myself. I've previously owned 5 Rolex's and therefore I'm familiar with what to expect when purchasing a Rolex either new or used and how it should arrive. With Watchfinder what started as a 5 star Trustpilot experience has turned into this. At the end of the day I purchased an expensive watch from Watchfinder if Watchfinder said to me the watch bezel will have to be cleaned when I receive it I wouldn't have paid the price I paid for what was advertised as a clean watch or I wouldn't have bought it and gone for another or purchased elsewhere, unfortunately I found out after payment. What a shame a great experience ended like this.My advise to anyone thinking of buying from Watchfinder is firstly make sure the watch is as described though in my case I asked twice and it still arrived requiring cleaning, MORE IMPORTANTLY IF PART EXCHANGING A WATCH VIA THE POST MAKE SURE YOUR HOUSE INSURANCE COVERS IT WHILST IN THE POST I'M PRETTY SURE IT WON'T.RESPONSE TO WATCHFINDERS REPLY DATED 5/6/15Thank you for your reply, the general condition of the watch in question on arrival was good. The contaminated bezel engravings given the promises made that it would be cleaned properly is both unprofessional and unsatisfactory for an expensive 6mth old prestige watch of value £5000+. I base this comment on the 5 other new/used Rolex watch purchases I've made over the years.I take exception to being told how house insurance works. My watches are identified on my policy for cover home/away and accidental but as with the majority of policies items of value over aprox £5000 have endorsements applied like the following pasted from my policy:FG24. Jewellery ClauseSection 2 (Contents) and Section 5 (Valuables and Personal Possessions) excludes Theft and DIsappearance of specified jewellery unless the jewellery is either:(a) Being worn by you, or(b) Deposited in a bank, locked safe, or(c) Carried by hand under your personal supervision.I have serious reservations over the ethics around Watchfinder advising customers their house insurance will cover postal insurance short falls which is why I've advised they check the endorsements on their policy.I was fully aware that by posting my part ex watch I was taking a risk but appreciated that was my responsibility. Returning the defective watch because Watchfinder didn't clean it properly is Watchfinders responsibility.Yes you have given me three solutions all of which entail me returning the watch under insured. I buy and sell on Ebay and have experienced items being lost in the post and the postal insurance not covering item value, I'm not about to take the same risk with a £5000+ watch due to a fault of Watchfinders making.When I purchased this watch I did so knowing of the insurance issue should I have to return it but based on two promises from Watchfinder that the watch had been cleaned and my previous experiences with Rolex high quality I didn't anticipate having to return it. The fact of the matter is contrary to promises made by Watchfinder the watch wasn't cleaned properly and therefore through Watchfinder's fault I have to return the watch under insured which is neither my fault or the fault of Rolex quality.I live to far from Watchfinder in London for it to be cost effective or practical to return the watch in person as suggested. I happened to be in London on other business when I paid them a visit as I was passing through Bank underground station on return from Canary Warf. At this point I have no more planned visits to London.You've asked how I plan to proceed, as returning the watch under insured isn't an option I appear to have no option but to keep it and clean it myself once I find out how, the suggestion made by Watchfinder that I may be able to remove the contamination in the bezel engravings with a wooden toothpick is a little worrying as the engravings are highlighted with platinum and I don't know if this would cause damage. The price I purchased this watch for is £120 less than other online retailers are selling the same watch brand new with stickers for with the same offered for my watch I now wonder if paying the additional £120 would have been the better option. I decided Watchfinders 6mth old watch would be as described and therefore a good option. If the watch had arrived cleaned as promised I would have been delighted and left glowing 5 star feedback but it didn't arrive cleaned as promised. As trivial as a contaminated bezel may appear to Watchfinder we are talking about a prestige watch of value £5000+.FURTHER REPLY TO WATCHFINDERReference your reply I’m sorry you see things this way, to clarify matters it’s not a case of me being unprepared to resolve this matter amicably but more a case of protecting my interest. Your idea of what’s amicable and mine differ which is understandable as you have Watchfinder’s interests at heart and I have to look after myself.Watchfinder declined my suggestion I have the watch cleaned by Rolex at your cost which would have been an amicable solution alternatively another amicable solution is reduce the price I paid to reflect it not arriving in the condition advertised and I’ll sort out the cleaning. We recommend you use a tracked mail system and retain proof of postage. You must insure the Goods to their FULL value. You must ensure that you pack the Goods appropriately to prevent damage during transit". Your own terms and conditions suggest it's inappropriate to advise customers send faulty watches to you using under insured postal services assuming their house insurance covers the uninsured sum.Once again thankyou for your assistance.

UPDATE:  I have discovered that despite being advertised as stickered,  unworn and with papers,  my Rolex Daytona did not have the user guide.   I did query this at the time and was told no user guide came with the watch.   I have since seen the user guide on photos of other similiar watches advertised.   After contacting them I have today received an email stating they are unable to locate a hard copy and have forwarded a pdf instead!   Not what I would expect from a company selling items as a financial investment.   I have recontacted them stating the guide is needed so lets hope they fulfill the 'with papers'  as advertised.I have been a keen watch owner since my first Omega almost 20 years ago.  I have added a Breitling to my collection and have been in the market for a Rolex.  I used the Watchfinder site to review details on pricing together with age and condition and after also reading information elsewhere on the internet settled on a Rolex Daytona based on its history and rarity.  I found that Watchfinder had the most available to view and comparisons with other sites showed the price to be very comparable.  I contacted Watchfinder to request a viewing at the exchange of 3 Rolex Daytona's and a Panarei for comparison.  I was called shortly after emailing the request by Keiran who confirmed that the Exchange was closed on the Saturday but could make the watches available for viewing at either Maidstone or Bluewater.  I agreed on Bluewater and attended the viewing.  The shop at Bluewater was very small however the watches requested were all available for viewing and Amy who assisted me was very helpful and friendly with nothing being too much trouble.  I decided on one of the Rolex Daytona's (all were in top condition with box and papers and stickered) and the strap was adjusted to suit as unlike many, I like to wear my watches with pride.  An hour after walking in I was walking out with the Daytona on my wrist  (ok it was set to the wrong time but it gave me something to fiddle with when I arrived home).  The watches were excellent, phone and email communications were excellent and I wouldnt hesitate to recommend Watchfinder. UPDATE: I now need to reserve jusgement after finding out the  user guide that should have been supplied was omitted from my purchase after also confirming none was supplied as part of a purchase from Rolex.

I saw a watch that I was interested in on the website. I arrived at the Bluewater store and was greeted quickly and warmly by Ashley. She was very friendly and we discussed different models of Rolex.The particular model I was interested in was in The Royal Exchange store (REX). I was informed that they were unable to hold the watch for me unless I had bought it. I purchased the watch as Ashley had allowed me to try on similar models.An appointment was arranged for me to collect the Rolex at 16.30, the next day, at The REX.I cannot fault their professionalism and I would certainly recommend the Bluewater Watch Finder to a friend.However, when I arrived (10 minutes) early to collect my £3350 Rolex at the REX store, I was not greeted or even acknowledged until 17.10. There was four members of staff available and dealing with customers. Customers that walked in after me were greeted before me. I was standing in view but ignored. I'm not sure if it was because I'm a young girl?When I finally was seen, I explained that I was here to collect my watch. I handed over my receipt and the store assistant went to collect it for me. I waited another 10 minutes for him to return.There was a mirrored door, where the staff would enter into the store room. I could clearly see, all but one member or staff laughing and talking, even eating. Bearing in mind that the time was 17.20ish and the shop was due to close at 17.30, I doubt very much they were on a break.When he returned with my watch, I tried it on and it was too loose. I requested that he take out some links for me. He rolled his eyes and let out a large sigh. He stalked off, snatching the watch.When he returned again, he bought the box with the watch in it. He did not communicate with me, apart from saying, 'Was there anything else?'. I replied, 'May I at least have a bag?'. Another eye rolling moment later, he handed me the bag for me to struggle, while juggling my other bags, to put my purchase into the bag myself.After receiving such excellent customer service from the Bluewater store, I expected consistency.As it turns out, I was not happy with the watch, I decided that I preferred the Rolex I tried on in the Bluewater store. I did not feel comfortable explaining that to the staff at REX. So I returned to Bluewater the next day to exchange. I feel I was only allowed to do this as the watch I wanted to exchange it for was £1500 dearer. I was also handed a 1 year Warranty. I did not receive this at REX.I paid thousands of pounds for a watch. The service I received was disgusting. Unacceptable. An embarrassment. I hope future customers do not make the mistake of using the REX Watch Finder. I certainly won't be holding back when asked for my opinion.

Having sent a watch that Watch Finder have retailing at £2000 and being offered £1200 on their online quoting system I sent my watch which is in better condition than the one on their site.After a confirmation e mail of receipt I then got a offer of £500 .Avoid if you are looking to sell a watch you will get a better offer from a local jeweller.

Great shop with competitive prices but Christmas week and at lunch time proved to be a hectic experience.Realistically more staff at peak times would go some way to a more relaxed experienceThat said the shop assistant proved helpful and professional, closing the deal on 2 beautiful Rolex watches.

Cannot fault the watch Omega seamaster professional simply brilliant. My only complaint advertised as next day however after 2 days I had to contact to track my order. I had no e mail to confirm full payment. Then when I got the watch, there wasnt even a cover letter. Not even a letter of info of my warranty. I found your company very aloof. Though I am happy with the watch, I think customer services could be improved!

My experience with Watch finder was spoilt by some un cooperate staff.Recommended by Father in law who has used them a few times, it started well so I decided to go ahead with what should have been a smooth and simple purchase.Well you would have thought so!! Used a while back to sell a Breitling.  Was told costs are a maximum of x.   Then when I got there I am told costs are subject to a minimum of y.    So ended up paying at least double the costs/fees I expected to or maybe more - can't quite recall the details as it was around 2010 or earlier.

A really good experience in buying the watch at a good saving but when it came to ask for a receipt for insurance purposes then absolutely no response to e-mails or phone calls & after 12 months I give up asking !

My 2002 sub is great but I feel that Watchfinder have squeezed an extra £100 from myself and that has left me with a slight bad taste!!!

I much preferred the old web site where a discounted guide price was displayed when enquiring about new watches. The current process of call back is in my opinion placing a unnecessary hurdle in the way which in todays world of immediate communication is frustrating. Although I have no qualms about the quality of the watch that I purchased I do have major concerns about how the purchase progressed. My wife initially dealt with ordering the watch and was quoted a price, she not only wrote this down for me but had two subsequent conversations with the sales representative to conform the price, as did my daughter who the watch was for.On arranging to transfer the money to conclude the purchase the price suddenly increased by several hundred pounds, the original  sales representative was no longer available and when they tracked him down he had no recollection of the telephone calls he had held with my wife and daughter.My daughter's heart was set on the watch and had it not been for that we would not have purchased but we did and had to pay the higher price.As "watchfinder" said to me in response to my complaints you should have got the purchase price in writing -so I'm doing them a favour by passing this advice on.

I have now bought 2 watches from watchfinder. The first was a one year old omega so it kept time perfectly. The second was a 9 year old tag which sadly did not! Lost 2 minutes per day. Sent it back for servicing and then decided to swap for a 9 year old breitling instead. I was pleased with the service given at the start when I purchased my watch, but disappointed that the watch lost value in a short time when asked about selling, no reason why given.A ongoing improvement would to explain why the price offered is given...

Watch arrived looking absolutely amazing, worked brilliantly...for about 7 months until it crashed, loosing all functions and abilities. WF have confirmed it has been recieved and sent to their Breitling experts, i have another week until i find out the diagnosis/resolution. Well, I have mixed feelings on Watchfinder. I initially bought a TAG from them in November 2011, customer service was great, delivery very fast and the watch had been re-finished to a high standard and looked as good as new. After wearing the watch for a week the watch had timing issues and kept stopping, no matter how many times I wound the movent or wore the watch it just kept stopping. Disappointing, especially when watchfinder are supposed to supply each watch with a full service which would have highlighted any issue with the movement. I returned the watch and they were happy to replace with a new watch, which was newer for the same price which i must admit was excellent service.After owning this watch for 3 months I decided it wasn't for me and made enquiries into exchanging the watch for a Rolex submariner. The trade in value they offered was ridiculous, I understand things depreciate and they need to turn a profit but to lose 50% of its value in 3 months on a second watch was harsh (the whole idea of buying second hand was to eleminate this depreciation). Then came the negotiation on the cost to change to a Rolex, I work in sales and when speaking to the sales advisor Alex, I was given little to no discount, especially as I was a returning customer, I did not want a lot of money off the watch, just a  gesture of goodwill. Instead he didn't reply to my email, so I actually went to Goldsmiths and bought a brand new Rolex GMTIIC in which I am chuffed to bits with. On the whole a mixed experience with Watchfinder, I don't think I would return.

A trouble free and pleasant experience until I met the 'buyer' of my Cartier who reduced the phone quote by £250 and was so rude, self opinionated and objectionable I was literally on the point of leaving - had it not been for the professionalism of the 'seller' of the Franck Muller who saved the day!If you operate a 'good cop bad cop' routine there it's working. If you don't then the 'buyer' needs some people skills, urgently.I will use you again, but keep that person away from me!The 'Muller is wonderful. It was valued for insurance purposes at£14,500

On the plus side,Natalie in service is an absolute treasure,I think she is about as good as you could possibly want from a back up service,so thank you Natalie.On the minus side,my Rolex has been back twice in the year since purchase and when I tried to trade it back in against a better model ,was told I had lost £700 on a £2400 watch in 7 months,would you be happy with this ????,regards Phil Taylor.

Was pleased to find the watch I wanted at a discount price from what I had seen in department stores. Although this is in their terms and conditions that it might happen I still was a bit surprised when it happened to me.

I purchased in 2012 a Breitling and after collecting it and having been promised that the watch was serviced and guaranteed i took it back with me to Turkey were i live,  in less than 3 months the watch was already defective and after being told i was to pay the costs for sending it for repair and also for returning it to be sent to Turkey,  including all taxes and duties i decided to have it repaired locally in Turkey due to the costs spiralling out of control if i would have sent it to the UK.It isnt so much the fact the watch was defective, but it was that it was less than 3 months of ownership and that for me based on a watch with a value of 1850 poiunds strikes to me that i really wonder if there had been any service as i know how i treated the watch in my ownership very carefully.

I find the first time buys from  Watchfinder to be excelent deals. But they are not so generous with part exchange if at a later date you want to upgrade to a more expensive watch. I believe they would do far more business with beter trade in prices.

Experience on purchase good, attended your premises and bought from there. I ended up buying from an alternate site. Disappointing as the web portal and initial contact experience was great.

I enjoy purchasing from Watchfinder, but not selling. I have bought and sold several watches now and on all (despite them all being in fantastic condition) the final offer price was in the middle or lower of that initially quoted as a guide. I do not believe that the top offer price quoted is EVER achievable... unless the watch has NEVER been worn (which, lets face it is not going to be the case for 99.99% of watches)My main issue:1 of the watches i sold was an Omega Planet Ocean. It was immaculate and keeping PERFECT time. However when it reached you it was apparently 'Magnetised' and therefore you apparently had to send it away to Omega to be de-magetised. This was apparently worth £200 less in your final price (the reason being that you would have to send it to Omega and this would take several weeks in which you clearly couldnt sell the watch). I reluctantly accepted this.HOWEVER the very next day my Planet Ocean was advertised and the following day it was SOLD. The same day i had an email saying you were now an authorised Omega service centre! I called up pretending to be an interested customer for my Omega, and was told it was with the servicing dept and would be back in a couple of days. YOU THEREFORE DELIBERATELY LIED TO ME IN ORDER TO GET THE PRICE DOWN. You knew at the time of the offer you could de-magnetise it yourselves very quickly and sell it.I will not be using Watchfinder again until i am compensated in some way.In addiition, i have now done some research and found that all OMEGA watches are anti-magnetic in accordance with the definitions of the ISO 764 standard anyway. Was my watch actually ever maganetised i wonder...

I did communicate this to them by phone and e-mail during the process.Would I use them again....maybe.
The initial contact was swift and helpful, but after sales was poor. I am still waiting for a response from 2 e-mailed questions, and my online account seems to no longer exist.

i was told 800/900 should have known it would be lower pricewas told can only give you £800 because watch needed adjusting.should i pay for you to adjust the watch you are buying.tell people before hand thats the only fault.

A few issues - the website payment service failed, the correction to my postal address was ignored, they used my work e-mail in error and the box the watch arrived in did not relate to the watch I bought. I am pleased with the watch.

When I bought my Rolex I was promised a written valuation for the watch & also I agreed that a valuation would be provided for another Rolex watch that I took with me. I received neither valuation despite phone calls & emails. However I am very satisfied with the watch that I bought.
